messages.subject: Infinite value after imputation
parts:
Dear MSstats team:

I got two questions about the imputation. 

1. After imputation (data.name.TMP <- dataProcess (raw = data.name, fillIncompleteRows = TRUE, normalization = "equalizeMedians", summaryMethod = "TMP", censoredInt = "NA", cutoffCensored = "minFeature", MBimpute= TRUE), I think I am doing the right thing?

However, after exported the tablet to excel, I found some proteins has the Log2FC label of "inf" and MissingPercentage >0.5. I know this is because the intensity is missing in one condition. 
The question is, I thought with imputation, a value should be give to those "0" intensity, so a proper pvalue or FDR and FC can be performed? 

2. If this is what it is, is it valid to use these proteins as our targets, saying with MissingPercentage<0.5, with infinity log2FC value? Can they still be considered as found in one condition, while not in the other OR they can only be used as outliers?

Thanks a lot for your help and look forward your reply.
Best
Cheng

messages.author: 2889aa2e61425c8e
messages.subject: Re: Infinite value after imputation
parts:
Dear Cheng,

We only impute missing values in a run if we observed at least one feature in that run. If the protein was not at all found in a run we leave the intensities in that run missing. When the protein is present in one condition but completely absent in all the runs in another condition, formal statistical inference cannot be performed. In these cases we set log2FC to infinity, and p-value to 0 without performing the tests. This is to avoid losing the proteins that can be biologically meaningful. So yes, you can use these proteins as targets for follow-up, as long as you can reliably identify them in at least one condition.

HTH
Olga
